title: Savoury baked oats with ham, leek and Bramley

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Oats, eggs, milk, cooked ham, Cheddar, wholegrain mustard and fresh produce are all plain kitchen staples with no factory-made sauces or mixes.

supermarket.reason: Every ingredient, including Bramleys and cooked ham, is an everyday item at any mainstream UK supermarket.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a baking dish, bowl, whisk and grater, and the technique is just mixing and baking.

works.reason: 200g oats to 400ml milk, 3 eggs and two grated Bramleys should set well in 30 to 35 minutes at 180°C fan, giving four generous portions with enough seasoning from the ham, mustard and Cheddar.

honest_times.reason: Fifteen minutes covers slicing a leek, grating apples and cheese and dicing ham, some of it done while the leek roasts, and the 10 minutes plus 30 to 35 minutes matches the 45 minutes of cooking.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning, including the fresh thyme, appears in the steps, nothing unlisted is used, and each name matches its id.

seasonal_feel.reason: A hot, cheesy baked oat dish with ham, leek and two grated Bramleys suits a December morning, and the apple is a main component rather than a garnish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, clear and in plain British English, with no restaurant language or preaching.

hearty_healthy.reason: Oats, eggs, ham, cheese, leek and apple make a filling, balanced savoury breakfast a family would happily eat again.
